title: CPU engine with libomp (2 threads)
hypothesis: The installed engine was single-threaded; libomp should let it use more cores.
conclusion: Measured 0.10 tok/s, but Colibri only used 2 threads on the M6 (see threads). Reference point for the GPU steps.

title: Metal GPU backend
hypothesis: Expert math and attention were on the CPU; the GPU was idle.
conclusion: Expert math and attention moved to the GPU; the SSD became the largest cost.

title: Overlap SSD reads with GPU work
hypothesis: Reads and math happen one after the other; overlapping should hide some read time.
conclusion: Small gain within noise on its own; kept because it combines with DIRECT.

title: Uncached SSD reads
hypothesis: Reading around the page cache avoids a copy and enables zero-copy GPU buffers.
conclusion: Faster; Colibri reports DIRECT can be drive-dependent.

title: Metal residency set
hypothesis: Registering resident buffers once should cut per-dispatch GPU scheduling overhead.
conclusion: Attention time fell sharply; GPU scheduling overhead mostly gone.

title: GPU keep-alive spin
hypothesis: A spinning GPU keep-alive should reduce dispatch latency.
conclusion: Faster.
tradeoffs: Uses more power; drop on battery.

title: Best exact combination
hypothesis: The residency set and the spin target different overheads, so they should add up.
conclusion: 0.43-0.44 tok/s, identical text, about 76% of time now waiting on the SSD.

title: 4 SSD readers instead of 8
hypothesis: Fewer readers might reduce contention.
conclusion: Within noise of 8 readers; the SSD is the limit, not the reader count.

title: 2 SSD readers
hypothesis: iobench saturates at 2 readers.
conclusion: No change.

title: 16 SSD readers
hypothesis: More queue depth might help the SSD.
conclusion: No change.

title: Cross-layer expert prefetch
hypothesis: Loading the next layer's likely experts early should hide read time.
conclusion: Hit rate rose to 10% but speed did not; most prefetched loads were discarded.

title: Page cache as the expert cache
hypothesis: Letting macOS cache experts might use free RAM better than slabs.
conclusion: GPU out-of-memory errors on every block; stopped.

title: Expert cache not wired into RAM
hypothesis: Wiring may not matter with a tiny cache.
conclusion: Refused to start: free RAM had dropped to 12.2 GB right after the mmap failure. Inconclusive; retry on a quiet machine.

title: 2 cache slots per layer (RAM 20 GB)
hypothesis: Doubling the expert cache should raise the hit rate.
conclusion: Hit rate 2% to 4%; too small to matter. A useful cache needs tens of GB.

title: CPU-only: 6 threads instead of 2
hypothesis: Colibri uses only the M6's 2 "Super" cores (colibri#2194).
conclusion: CPU math and prompt reading scale with cores.

title: CPU-only: 12 threads instead of 2
hypothesis: Colibri uses only the M6's 2 "Super" cores (colibri#2194).
conclusion: CPU math and prompt reading scale with cores.
tradeoffs: Efficiency cores add heat; 6 vs 12 differences are small.

title: Metal exact: 6 threads instead of 2
hypothesis: Colibri uses only the M6's 2 "Super" cores (colibri#2194).
conclusion: No change: exact Metal runs wait on the SSD.

title: Metal exact: 12 threads instead of 2
hypothesis: Colibri uses only the M6's 2 "Super" cores (colibri#2194).
conclusion: No change: exact Metal runs wait on the SSD.
tradeoffs: Efficiency cores add heat; 6 vs 12 differences are small.

title: Metal skip < 0.5: 6 threads instead of 2
hypothesis: Colibri uses only the M6's 2 "Super" cores (colibri#2194).
conclusion: CPU-side overhead fell from 26% to ~9-12% of each token.

title: Metal skip < 0.5: 12 threads instead of 2
hypothesis: Colibri uses only the M6's 2 "Super" cores (colibri#2194).
conclusion: CPU-side overhead fell from 26% to ~9-12% of each token.
tradeoffs: Efficiency cores add heat; 6 vs 12 differences are small.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.03
hypothesis: Skipping low-weight experts that are not in RAM avoids SSD reads.
conclusion: Skipped almost nothing; identical text.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.05
hypothesis: Skipping low-weight experts that are not in RAM avoids SSD reads.
conclusion: Skipped almost nothing; identical text.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.10
hypothesis: Skipping low-weight experts that are not in RAM avoids SSD reads.
conclusion: Skipped <1% of loads; identical text.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.20
hypothesis: Skipping low-weight experts that are not in RAM avoids SSD reads.
conclusion: ~25% of loads skipped; reworded, still correct.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.30

conclusion: ~60% skipped; reworded, still correct.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.40

conclusion: ~77% skipped; reworded, still correct.

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.50

title: Skip missed experts below weight 0.70

title: Skip missed experts below weight 1.0
hypothesis: Skipping low-weight experts that are not in RAM avoids SSD reads.
conclusion: Output loops ("and the air, and the air"). Breaking point.

title: Code prompt: skip below 0.20
hypothesis: Check the skip trade-off on a code answer.
conclusion: Same function structure through 0.30; reworded at 0.50.

title: Code prompt: skip below 0.30
hypothesis: Check the skip trade-off on a code answer.
conclusion: Same function structure through 0.30; reworded at 0.50.

title: Code prompt: skip below 0.50
hypothesis: Check the skip trade-off on a code answer.
conclusion: Same function structure through 0.30; reworded at 0.50.

title: Cache-aware routing
hypothesis: Swap low-ranked experts for ones already in RAM.
conclusion: 0% swapped: with ~1 slot per layer there is nothing in RAM to swap to.

title: Cache-aware routing, wider window
hypothesis: A wider window might find more cached experts.
conclusion: Same as default: nothing to swap to.

title: Skip < 0.10 plus cache-aware routing
hypothesis: Combine both lossy levers.
conclusion: Same as skip < 0.10 alone.

title: Vulkan dense chain, experts on CPU
change: VK=1 build, COLI_VULKAN=1 COLI_VK_CHAIN=1 (+ MoltenVK patch)
hypothesis: Keeping whole layers on the GPU avoids per-layer CPU round trips.
conclusion: Expert math stayed on the CPU (71% of time); prompt reading 3x slower.
tradeoffs: Needs MoltenVK and a portability patch.

title: Vulkan chain + 3 GB GPU expert tier
hypothesis: Put routed experts on the GPU too.
conclusion: Only ~3% of experts reached the GPU tier.

title: Vulkan chain + tier, skip < 0.5
hypothesis: Lossy mode is attention-bound, where the chain should help most.
conclusion: Slower than Metal at the same threshold.

title: Vulkan chain + Metal experts, skip < 0.5
hypothesis: Chain for dense work, Metal for experts.
conclusion: Chain attention took 78% of time; prompt reading 154 s.

title: GPU prompt reading
hypothesis: Prompt reading runs attention on the CPU; the GPU should be faster. Not bit-exact by design.
conclusion: Prompt reading time unchanged (23.5 s vs 23.2 s): it is bound by expert reads, not attention. Generation was 16% slower in this single run, but the code-prompt run saw no change, so treat that as noise or as an effect on draft-verify steps. Not worth using.

title: GPU prompt reading, code prompt
hypothesis: Same, with a longer prompt.
conclusion: No change (32.3 s vs 32.2 s).

title: Skip below 0.30 with 12 threads
hypothesis: Lossy runs spend more time on CPU-side work, which more threads should cut.
conclusion: No change: at 0.30 the run is still mostly waiting on the SSD.

title: Skip below 0.40 with 12 threads
hypothesis: Lossy runs spend more time on CPU-side work, which more threads should cut.
conclusion: Small gain within noise.

title: Skip below 0.50 with 12 threads
hypothesis: Lossy runs spend more time on CPU-side work, which more threads should cut.
conclusion: Faster: with most reads skipped, CPU-side work is the bottleneck that threads remove.

title: Second SSD for expert reads
hypothesis: Exact runs are SSD-bound; splitting reads across two drives could nearly double read speed.
conclusion: Not run: needs an external NVMe drive.

title: Lossless compressed experts (int4-rans256-g0)
hypothesis: ~24% fewer bytes to read with byte-exact output.
conclusion: Not run: Colibri has the codec but no engine loader yet; CPU decoding would likely cost what it saves.

title: REAP expert pruning
hypothesis: A smaller model raises the cache hit rate.
conclusion: Not run: still 8 experts per token, so bytes per token stay the same; community GLM cards report quality loss at 34%.

title: 3-bit or mixed-precision experts
hypothesis: int3 cuts expert bytes ~25%.
conclusion: Not run: lossy and needs re-converting 409 GB; papers report large losses at 2-bit.

title: Terse prompting ("answer as briefly as possible")
hypothesis: Shorter answers finish sooner even at the same tok/s, if accuracy holds.
conclusion: Running in the quality bench (glm_bench.py v1).
